beats.beat: The company processes and sells four categories of chemicals: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are specialty chemicals used across industries.
It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell products through the promoter's network. This relationship is a key dependency.
Top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka. Exports totalled ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.

Competitive strengths cited include a diversified product portfolio, serving diversified user industries, import substitution potential, support from the holding company, and a focus on product innovation through continuous R&D.

beats.beat: Promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (corporate promoter). They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up capital.
The Promoter Group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 equity shares (0.24%).

Related party transactions exist for the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18. The company acknowledges it may continue such transactions.

The company has not yet obtained certain statutory licenses for one of its manufacturing facilities (Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara). There have also been instances of non-filing/delays in statutory filings with the RoC.

beats.beat: India's specialty chemicals industry (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, growing at a 10-12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017.
CRISIL Research forecasts the segment to grow at 12-14% CAGR going forward. Sub-segments like construction chemicals and water chemicals are expected to grow even faster at 15% CAGR.
The industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs accounting for 70-75% of market share. Only a few Indian players can compete globally on product development and innovation.

Growth drivers include increased consumption intensity, rising GDP and middle-class households (expected 148 million by 2030), government initiatives like the Draft National Chemical Policy, and 100% FDI allowance in the sector.
Stricter environmental regulations in China since 2015 have reduced output there, creating opportunities for Indian specialty chemical makers through import substitution.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited is a specialty chemicals processor that sells functional additives, chemically modified minerals, and soft/hard minerals. It relies on a long-term distribution arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.

The company is raising funds through a fresh issue of equity shares to be listed on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it plans to raise, and the listing venue.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale is mentioned in the DRHP). It will list on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).

Objects of the issue: (i) funding capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (ii) general corporate purposes; and (iii) creating a public trading market for the shares and enhancing visibility.
Lead manager: Vivro Financial Services Private Limited. Registrar: Link Intime India Private Limited.

beats.beat: Customer and supplier risk: The company has no long-term agreements with customers or raw material suppliers; sales are governed by purchase orders and raw material procurement is on a spot basis. This exposes revenue and margins to sudden changes.
Negative cash flows: In FY2017, net cash flow from operations was negative ₹349.75 lakh. Although other years were positive, a recurrence could strain growth and liquidity.

Regulatory non-compliance: The company has not obtained all required licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara. It also has a history of delayed or incorrect filings with the RoC.
Intense competition: The specialty chemicals industry is highly fragmented with SMEs holding 70-75% market share. Global players also compete, creating pricing pressure.

Related party concentration: The company's business model depends on a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, for marketing and sales. Any disruption to this relationship would materially affect revenue.
